1.42 Re-add Cloud indexes at every launch without disturbing the app

Symptom. Sync-status panels, cache-size checks and settings cleanup run queries that take seconds each on a large Cloud library. Indexes fix them, but Cloud deletes undeclared indexes at every launch.

Prerequisites. A backup of Lightroom Library.lrlibrary taken while Cloud is quit. Statistics from ANALYZE asset_sync_status_ui (they persist). Read Cloud indexes first.

Method. freeze_build.py waits for 30 s without database changes, freezes Cloud with SIGSTOP, takes the write lock without waiting, builds one index, commits and resumes Cloud, with an independent resume timer as a backstop. index_renewal.py runs this once per launch from a LaunchAgent, after a 90 s settle and an APFS-clone rollback.

Verification. Each query returns identical typed results with the index and with NOT INDEXED in one snapshot. Cloud’s console log shows no “database is locked” lines.

Evidence. Two live runs froze Cloud for 2.3–10.5 s per index with zero lock errors. Cache-size queries dropped to milliseconds. A third index that sped up sync-status queries (1.5 s to 0.0001 s) was withdrawn: Lightroom’s photo-list status lookup picked it and took 10.7 s, which triggered Versions timeouts when opening photos. Check every query on a table before adding an index to it.

Undo. Unload the LaunchAgent and restart Cloud, which deletes the indexes.

Limits. This is an external write to a live Adobe database and is not supported by Adobe. Each extra index slows Cloud’s own writes slightly.
